title: DeepSeek Wrapping Up Reported $15 Billion Round Led by Tencent and CATL
excerpt: Reuters' sources put the round at about 100 billion yuan ($14.98 billion), double the original target, with CATL and Tencent among the biggest investors — but the deal is not yet complete, its details could change, and none of the companies has confirmed it.
body:
• DeepSeek is wrapping up a funding round of about 100 billion yuan ($14.98 billion), two people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters — double its original 50 billion yuan target.
  • Battery maker CATL and WeChat operator Tencent Holdings were among the biggest investors, according to one of the people; Bloomberg first reported the $15 billion figure on Thursday.
  • The round is set to complete in the coming days, but the details are not final and could still change, and none of DeepSeek, CATL or Tencent commented — the figure is reported, not company-confirmed.
  • For tech readers, the signal is scale: a Chinese lab raising at this level, after hiring CITIC Securities in September to prepare for a possible STAR Market listing, narrows the funding gap with leading US labs.

Chinese AI startup DeepSeek is wrapping up its latest funding round having generated about 100 billion yuan ($14.98 billion) from existing and new investors, two people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters on Thursday. Battery maker Contemporary Amperex Technology (CATL) and WeChat operator Tencent Holdings were among the biggest investors in the round, one of the people said. Both people declined to be named because the information was confidential.

Bloomberg first reported the round on Thursday, saying DeepSeek had raised $15 billion with CATL and Tencent as its main backers, a version carried by The Economic Times. Reuters' own sourcing broadly matches that account on the amount and the two lead investors — but the two reports differ on status, and the difference matters: Bloomberg's version describes money raised, while Reuters' sources describe a round still being completed.

What Is Verified, and What Is Not

Three elements are supported by both reports: the size, at about 100 billion yuan or roughly $15 billion; the identity of CATL and Tencent as among the biggest investors; and the fact that the round doubled DeepSeek's original fundraising target of 50 billion yuan. Reuters put the exchange rate at $1 to 6.6749 yuan, which makes 100 billion yuan equal to $14.98 billion.

What is not established is a closed, confirmed transaction. Reuters reported that the fundraising is set to be complete in the coming days, but that financial details are not ironclad and could still change. DeepSeek, CATL and Tencent could not immediately be reached for comment, and none of the three has publicly confirmed the amount, a valuation, or individual commitments. No valuation for DeepSeek was given in either report. This article therefore treats the $15 billion as a figure reported by Bloomberg and corroborated in outline by Reuters' sources — not as a company-announced fact.

Why Investors Doubled the Target

The oversubscription itself is the story's clearest signal. DeepSeek will have doubled its original target, underscoring strong interest from investors — many backed by the state and big corporations — as China aims to get ahead in the AI race against the US, Reuters reported. A battery maker and a social-media and gaming giant leading a language-model round also shows how China's largest industrial and platform companies are positioning themselves inside the country's AI stack rather than only building their own models.

The fundraising also points towards public markets. In September, Reuters reported that DeepSeek had hired CITIC Securities to prepare for a potential initial public offering on Shanghai's STAR Market. A private round of this size, completed shortly after that appointment became known, reads as a pre-listing step as much as an operating raise.

The Product Behind the Valuation Story

Last month DeepSeek released its latest model, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, which it said was designed for greater capability, faster inference, higher throughput and scaling to larger models, according to Reuters. That release cadence — new models shipping while the company raises and prepares a listing — is the basis on which investors are being asked to treat a Hangzhou research lab as a peer to leading US labs rather than a low-cost challenger.

For Indian and diaspora technologists, the practical takeaway is competitive, not speculative: capital at this scale buys computing capacity and talent, the two inputs that determine how fast model quality converges. Until DeepSeek or its investors confirm the round's final terms, the precise number should be read with the caveat Reuters attached to it — expected in the coming days, and still subject to change.
